components.css: :host{--stage:#1d1647;--hud:#150f38;--panel:#251d5a;--panel-up:#2f2670;--line:#3b3185;--ink:#f8f4ff;--ink-2:#c4bcef;--ink-dark:#150f38;--coral:#ff5a36;--gold:#ffc42e;--mint:#2fd3a4;--blue:#4d7cff;--coral-deep:#b8331a;--gold-deep:#b5850a;--mint-deep:#138a69;--blue-deep:#2f4fc0;--r:14px;--r-lg:20px;--display:Unbounded,system-ui,sans-serif;--ease:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)} .ds-sheet{display:grid;gap:.55rem;padding:1.1rem 16px;color:var(--ink-dark);background:var(--mint);border-radius:var(--r-lg) var(--r-lg) 0 0;box-shadow:0 -12px 32px rgb(10 7 34 / .45);font:400 1rem/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif;animation:ds-rise .38s var(--ease)} .ds-judge{margin:0;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:.6rem;font:800 1.75rem/1 var(--display);letter-spacing:.04em;font-style:oblique 8deg;text-transform:uppercase;animation:ds-stamp .42s var(--ease) both} .ds-sheet p{margin:0} .ds-btn{min-height:48px;border:0;border-radius:var(--r);background:var(--ink-dark);color:var(--ink);font:700 1rem/1 var(--display);box-shadow:0 4px 0 #0a0722;cursor:pointer;transition:transform .08s,box-shadow .08s} .ds-btn:active{transform:translateY(4px);box-shadow:none} .ds-btn:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--ink-dark);outline-offset:3px} @keyframes ds-rise{from{transform:translateY(100%)}} @keyframes ds-stamp{from{transform:scale(1.5);opacity:0}} @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-sheet,.ds-judge{animation:none}}

narrative.overview:
Every review is a note you hit. Hub is a rhythm game's stage at night: a deep indigo floor, a darker HUD strip pinned to the top, raised indigo panels, and four lane colours that light up only when something is being played or judged. Answers sit in lanes, every hit gets a stamped judgement, and a finished day gets a grade.

The density is phone-first and thumb-sized: 48px buttons, 60px game and answer rows, one column under 860px, two above. Reading text stays in the system face; Unbounded carries numerals, headings, buttons and judgements, so the game voice and the reading voice never blur. Pressable things are chunky and physical: a solid bottom edge is the key travel, and it drops to zero on press.

The world borrows grammar from real rhythm-game results screens and Duolingo's lesson flow (top progress track, slide-up answer sheet, press-down buttons, stat tiles), translated into Hub's own indigo-and-lanes look, never copying game art.
keyCharacteristics: Dark indigo tonal layers (stage, HUD, panel, panel-up) instead of soft shadows.
Four lane colours with one meaning each: a lane, a game, a judgement, a grade.
Unbounded for numbers and the game voice; system UI for reading.
Press-down buttons with a solid bottom edge that travels on press.
Judgements are always word + icon + colour, stamped in.

rules.name: The Lane Meaning Rule
rules.body: Coral, gold, mint and blue only ever mean an answer lane, a game, a judgement (Perfect mint, Good gold, Miss coral) or a grade. Never use one for decoration, a primary action, or a generic status.

rules.name: The Ink Action Rule
rules.body: Primary buttons are ink with dark-ink text; secondary buttons are raised indigo. On a lane-coloured surface (the Starter) the action is the dark button.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Unbounded is for numbers, headings, buttons and judgements; anything the user reads to learn is system UI.

rules.name: The Key Travel Rule
rules.body: A solid bottom edge means "this can be pressed or this was stamped". It always collapses on press; it never appears on static panels.

dos: Do keep every lane colour tied to a lane, a game, a judgement or a grade: Perfect is mint, Good is gold, Miss is coral.
Do make primary buttons ink and secondary buttons raised indigo; use the dark button on a lane-coloured surface.
Do show every judgement as word + icon + colour, never colour alone.
Do start every run screen's single HUD row with the leave (X) button.
Do take icons from the inline Tabler outline sprite in index.html (2px stroke, round caps, currentColor).
Do collapse the solid bottom edge on press for anything that has one.
Do keep all animation behind prefers-reduced-motion.
donts: Don't put kicker or eyebrow labels above headings.
Don't use a lane colour for a primary action, decoration or general status.
Don't add type sizes beyond the three-step ramp except for display numerals.
Don't use emoji or text glyphs as icons.
Don't give static panels a bottom edge or soft shadow; the sheet is the only floating surface.
